title: Sunday Morning
excerpt: Complacencies of the peignoir, and late coffee and oranges
note: A Sunday poem about replacing inherited heaven with the difficult, sensuous world in front of you.
why: It sits exactly between religious-cultural analysis and lived appetite: belief, doubt, breakfast, mortality.

title: The Second Coming
excerpt: Things fall apart; the centre cannot hold
note: A compressed model of political and spiritual order breaking under historical strain.
why: It is overquoted because it keeps working: regime anxiety, religious imagination, and social fracture in one page.

title: The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock
excerpt: Let us go then, you and I
note: A poem of social paralysis, self-consciousness, and the interior cost of modern urban life.
why: Useful when the day needs a reminder that hesitation can become its own architecture.

title: Tell all the truth but tell it slant
excerpt: Tell all the truth but tell it slant
note: A tiny operating manual for truth, tact, and indirect illumination.
why: It fits a dashboard that needs to tell hard truths without becoming noisy or blunt.

title: God's Grandeur
excerpt: The world is charged with the grandeur of God
note: A religious poem that treats beauty as pressure in the physical world, not an abstraction.
why: Good for the religion/culture lane: doctrine, industry, nature, and perception in fourteen lines.

title: The Darkling Thrush
excerpt: I leant upon a coppice gate
note: A winter poem about exhausted civilization and a small, irrational note of hope.
why: It pairs political fatigue with attention: not optimism exactly, but a signal in the dusk.

title: London
excerpt: I wander thro' each charter'd street
note: A city poem where politics, markets, church, and family pain all show up as institutions.
why: A compact civic x-ray for days when the Society & Ideas lane needs bite.

title: Up-Hill
excerpt: Does the road wind up-hill all the way?
note: A call-and-response poem about endurance, rest, and the shape of a whole life.
why: Useful when the day needs spiritual gravity without sermonizing.

title: The World Is Too Much with Us
excerpt: The world is too much with us; late and soon
note: A complaint about commerce, attention, and spiritual numbness that still feels current.
why: A clean counterweight to market dashboards: money matters, but it can also flatten perception.
